stories.headline: Trump and AI chiefs sign ‘morally binding’ super-intelligence safety accord
stories.summary: After a White House lunch with Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Dario Amodei, Jensen Huang, Greg Brockman, Sundar Pichai and others, President Trump said the group signed a voluntary “super intelligence” accord he called “almost like a constitution” and “morally binding.” Speaker Mike Johnson cast it as a joint commitment to robust internal controls; the one-page text Trump posted commits firms to four layers of audits plus regular safety talks, and Trump said he will name an AI czar within days. Critics such as Sen. Mark Warner still want Congress to mandate testing rather than industry self-policing.

stories.headline: Trump to tout manufacturing boom at surprise Peterbilt stop in Denton, Texas
stories.summary: FOX Business reports President Trump will make a surprise Thursday stop at Peterbilt’s Denton, Texas factory to sell tariffs, deregulation, and an America First manufacturing pitch ahead of the midterms. The White House credits heavy-truck tariffs with Paccar adding more than 1,000 Denton jobs and 2,000 U.S. jobs; UAW’s Shawn Fain congratulated Trump for delivering for heavy-truck workers. Trump argues pledged investment will reverse manufacturing losses even as BLS still shows a net manufacturing job decline since January 2025.

stories.headline: Supreme Court lets Trump keep third-country deportations running for now
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday allowed the Trump administration to keep deporting people to countries other than their own while it weighs whether migrants must get a meaningful chance to object first. The order pauses an appeals-court block that federal lawyers said had already forced cancellation of a flight carrying about 70 people; justices previously let such flights continue last year. Under often-secret deals, the administration says it has sent some 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries — most to Mexico — when home countries will not take them back.

stories.headline: DOJ charges Venezuelan illegal alien shot by ICE after Austin chase
stories.summary: U.S. Attorney Justin Simmons announced that Wilber Rafael Garces-Perez, 28, a Venezuelan illegal alien under a final removal order, made his initial federal appearance Tuesday on one count of assaulting and resisting a federal officer — facing up to 20 years if convicted. The complaint says he ignored park-and-exit orders during a Sept. 20 ICE traffic stop, struck an officer with his side-view mirror while fleeing, led a high-speed chase, then allegedly tried to hit an officer again, prompting the shooting. A detention hearing is set for Oct. 2 under Operation Take Back America.

stories.headline: Jewish groups say Mamdani’s antisemitism plan ducks anti-Israel rhetoric
stories.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s long-awaited antisemitism strategy pledges $1M for synagogue security and $6.4M for Partners Against the Hate grants, plus Holocaust education and Jewish culture spending — but major Jewish groups including UJA-Federation, AJC NY, and the NY Board of Rabbis say it fails to confront anti-Israel rhetoric they argue fuels attacks. The plan refuses a single antisemitism definition after Mamdani revoked Adams’ IHRA order; ADL and Rabbi Rick Jacobs called that omission serious while Bend the Arc and Brad Lander praised the funding track.

stories.headline: Trumbull volleyball stays perfect 4–0 with 3–0 sweep of Ridgefield
stories.summary: Trumbull’s volleyball Eagles kept an undefeated season alive Monday with a decisive 3–0 win at Ridgefield (25-12, 25-19, 25-7), extending their streak over the Tigers to six straight and lifting Trumbull to 4–0. Ridgefield fell to 2–5 and has now lost seven straight at home dating to last season. Trumbull hits the road again Wednesday at Stamford at 4 p.m.; the full match is available on the NFHS Network.

stories.headline: Falcon Rep brings Mamet’s A Life in the Theatre to Trumbull Library Oct. 15–17
stories.summary: Trumbull-founded Falcon Repertory Company will stage a free concert reading of David Mamet’s A Life in the Theatre at the Trumbull Library Community Room on Thursday, Oct. 15 at 6 p.m. and Saturday, Oct. 17 at 2 p.m. Frank S. Petrilli directs Equity actors Raymond Gerard Michaud and Jeffrey F. Wright in the bittersweet two-hander about a veteran and a rookie backstage — a show the trio has already done in New Canaan and at Trumbull’s Pinebrook Theater. Admission is free; suggested for adults at 33 Quality Street.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo ‘Get Ready’ opens Oct. 12 ahead of scarce Oct. 16 pre-orders
stories.summary: Apple’s iPhone Duo product page now shows a Get Ready window starting Monday, Oct. 12 — letting buyers lock color, capacity, carrier, AppleCare+, trade-in, payment, and shipping so pre-orders can fire with one tap when they open Friday, Oct. 16 at 8 a.m. ET. With yields stuck near 60% and early stock expected to be tight, MacRumors notes Get Ready could matter more than usual before the $1,999 foldable launches Oct. 23.

stories.headline: Amazon expands first Ultra 4 cash discounts — select models at $779.99
stories.summary: Amazon widened its first cash discounts on brand-new Apple Watch Ultra 4 to three configs at $779.99 — $19 off the $799 list — including Natural Sand Trail Loop (M/L), Black Ocean Band, and Black Burgundy Trail Loop (M/L). Series 12 GPS also sees light $9 markdowns (42mm $389.99 / 46mm $439.99). Useful for readers who want new-gen Ultra toughness without waiting for deeper clearance.

stories.headline: Tesla doubles Austin Cybercab Robotaxi fleet to about 125 units
stories.summary: Tesla’s Robotaxi app notified Austin riders that the Cybercab fleet has doubled, with Teslarati tracking availability from about 58 units early last week to roughly 125 by Friday — expanding the steering-wheel-less, pedal-less two-seater inside the year-old Robotaxi service. Cybercab rides began in early September in Austin only, with wait times previously high; the jump is a confidence signal on FSD handling unsupervised rides even as NHTSA still presses for sworn Cybercab certification answers.

stories.headline: Jets open as 3-point underdogs at Bears after back-to-back heartbreakers
stories.summary: After a second straight devastating loss — Geno Smith strip-sacked by ex-Jet Chuck Clark inside the Lions’ 30 with the game tied late — the 1–2 Jets open as 3-point road underdogs at Chicago (+138 ML, 43.5 O/U on FanDuel). Chicago is also 1–2 and may still be without Caleb Williams after Tyson Bagent managed just three points vs. Minnesota; if Williams sits, Gang Green Nation argues the Jets’ path back to .500 gets clearer.

stories.headline: LEGO officially reveals first Dragon Ball set: Shenron & Kid Goku for $180
stories.summary: LEGO and Toei Animation officially unveiled Icons set 11390 Dragon Ball: Shenron & Goku — 1,764 pieces, Kid Goku minifigure, Dragon Balls diorama, standing over 12 inches — with Insiders early access Nov. 1 and general release Nov. 4 at $179.99. LEGO’s Federico Begher called it the start of a multi-year Dragon Ball partnership with more sets due in 2027, moving the earlier leak into confirmed shelf reality for adult builders.

stories.headline: Ohio Supreme Court: no plain error skipping transferred self-defense instruction
stories.summary: In a 6–1 ruling, the Supreme Court of Ohio upheld Timothy Bradley’s convictions for shooting into neighboring homes even though a jury acquitted him of felonious assault on a self-defense claim after he fired at contractor Zachary Burch. Justice Deters wrote that Bradley never requested a transferred-self-defense instruction, Ohio has never adopted that doctrine, and counsel already told jurors self-defense applied to all counts — so omitting a sua sponte transfer charge was not plain error. Justice Brunner dissented, saying the habitation statute’s “without privilege” element needed an explicit self-defense privilege explanation.
